knownConcerns.topic: p99 Latency Spikes during Database Migration
knownConcerns.description: Worried that upcoming Postgres schema migration will lock tables and spike latency past 150ms.
Needs hard evidence that Graviton arm64 instances reduce cloud spend by >20% to justify annual budget signoff.

preferences.text: Prefers crisp bulleted summaries and terminal metrics over slides.
Begins meetings by reviewing open commitments first.
Insists on exact CLI commands and config snippets for his SRE team.

recommendedQuestions.question: “Rahul, before we dive in, should we confirm the Graviton3 benchmark results showing 24% lower memory cost per query?”
recommendedQuestions.rationale: Directly resolves his CFO budget concern and honors his preference to review open commitments first.

recommendedQuestions.question: “For the October 15 schema migration window, would it help if we deploy an ephemeral routing buffer to absorb any 30-second Postgres locks?”
recommendedQuestions.rationale: Directly addresses his highest severity fear of p99 latency spikes during table migrations.

recommendedQuestions.question: “Has your SRE war room roster been finalized, or do we need to provide additional onboarding sessions for the 3 junior platform engineers?”

memorySources.meetingTitle: Q3 Architecture Review & Latency SLA Sync
memorySources.excerpt: Rahul: "My biggest worry isn’t steady state. It’s what happens during the October database schema migration when Postgres locks tables for 30 seconds. If your agent caches stale routing paths and latency jumps past 150ms, our mobile checkouts fail."
memorySources.whyItMatters: Rahul's biggest fear is checkout failure during the upcoming Oct 15 Postgres schema migration. Proving your routing cache absorbs 30s table locks without breaching the 150ms SLA eliminates his primary operational blocker.

memorySources.meetingTitle: Q3 Architecture Review & Latency SLA Sync
memorySources.excerpt: You: "We will benchmark our worker node throughput on AWS Graviton3 (c7g.4xlarge) compared to x86 and deliver the side-by-side memory bandwidth report before our next sync on October 2."
memorySources.whyItMatters: This commitment is due today. Presenting the 24% Graviton memory throughput gain directly resolves Rahul's need for hard ROI figures before he talks to the CFO.

memorySources.excerpt: Rahul: "Our CFO is auditing all infrastructure line items over $100k. I need to clearly prove to him that adopting this solution reduces our total EC2 footprint rather than adding another vanity layer."
memorySources.whyItMatters: Acme finance leadership is scrutinizing all enterprise tooling. Rahul is your champion, but he needs defensible cost-savings metrics to protect this deal against executive budget scrutiny.

memorySources.excerpt: Rahul: "Please don’t walk me through a 20-slide deck. Let’s look at the action items from last week first, then go straight into the live terminal test output."
memorySources.whyItMatters: Rahul has zero tolerance for fluff. Starting today's call with slide decks will frustrate him; starting with open commitments and live benchmark numbers establishes immediate credibility.

memorySources.meetingTitle: PoC Review & Edge Cache Architecture Evaluation
memorySources.excerpt: Rahul: "We strictly avoid vendor-locked binary formats. Everything interfacing with our logging cluster must serialize into standard JSON or OpenTelemetry protobuf format."
memorySources.whyItMatters: Acme's platform philosophy mandates vendor-neutral telemetry. Demonstrating open JSON/OTel export prevents compliance and architecture vetoes from his platform committee.

memorySources.excerpt: Rahul: "I appreciate direct answers. If a feature isn’t ready or if failover adds 20ms of jitter, just tell me upfront. We can engineer around known physics, but surprises burn trust."
memorySources.whyItMatters: Rahul values radical candor. Being transparent about known edge cases builds long-term executive trust and cements your status as a true technical partner rather than a vendor.
